property_summary: After any successful Put by any caller with any positive value, the caller's recorded balance in C increases by exactly the sent amount (i.e., Put always unlocks and updates balance so subsequent Put calls are allowed); the mutant that never resets locked_ can leave the contract permanently locked, causing subsequent Put calls to revert and thus breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero payable Put call, the reference contract always accepts the call (does not revert) and records the increased balance; the mutant that fails to reset locked_ can leave the contract permanently locked so some subsequent Put calls by any caller will revert, violating this universal acceptance property.

For any caller and any nonzero payable Put call from that caller when they have sufficient ETH, the reference contract always allows two sequential Put calls (both succeed) whereas the mutant that never resets the reentrancy lock can make the second Put revert; the test fuzzes an address and amount and asserts that two sequential Put calls both succeed on the reference.

The reference contract always allows a successful single Put call (it does not remain locked after completion), so after any single successful Put by an address, a subsequent Put by the same address (with any value) will also be allowed to execute (i.e. not revert); the mutant that never resets locked_ can cause the contract to remain locked after the first Put and make a subsequent Put revert for some inputs.

For any caller address A and any nonzero value v <= caller balance, performing Put(v) twice in a row (two separate transactions) on the reference always allows the second Put to execute (i.e. does not revert); the mutant that never clears the reentrancy lock can cause the contract to remain locked after the first Put so the second Put reverts for some inputs.

After any successful Put by any sender with any msg.value, the last logged History entry's Val equals the resulting stored Acc[sender].balance; the mutant logs the incoming msg.value before adding it to the stored balance, so for some inputs (nonzero prior balance) the logged Val will not equal the new stored balance.

After any Put by a sender, the Log's last recorded Val equals the holder's stored balance for that sender (i.e., the log records the post-call stored balance); the mutant logs msg.value before updating balance, so when prior balance>0 the logged Val will differ from the new stored balance.

For any sender and any payable amount where the sender's prior stored balance is zero, after calling Put the Log's last recorded Val equals the holder's stored balance; the mutant (which logs msg.value before updating balance) can violate this when prior balance > 0, so by fuzzing a prior deposit then a second Put with nonzero prior we can find a counterexample that breaks the mutant.

For any sender and any two sequential Put calls (first with amount a1, then with amount a2 and possibly updated unlockTime), the Log's last recorded Val after the second Put equals the holder's stored balance for that sender (i.e. the reference logs the post-update accumulated balance), but the mutant that logs msg.value before updating balance can make the logged Val (msg.value) differ from the new accumulated balance when the prior balance is nonzero.

For any sender and any payable Put(amount) call, the reference C always records in Log.History the logged Val equal to the resulting holder's Acc[sender].balance after the call completes; the mutant which logs msg.value before updating the stored balance will violate this for some inputs where the sender had a prior nonzero balance.
Collect cannot withdraw funds when the holder's balance is below MinSum even if requested amount <= balance and unlockTime passed.
Collect should never revert when the caller's recorded balance is at least MinSum, at least the requested amount, and the unlock time has passed.
If the caller has previously deposited at least MinSum and the unlockTime has passed, then calling Collect for an amount <= that recorded balance must not revert.

If caller's recorded balance is at least the requested amount and the unlockTime has passed, Collect must not revert (i.e., original requires MinSum but we strengthen inputs so caller's recorded balance is >= MinSum).
If the caller has previously deposited at least MinSum and the unlock time has passed, then calling Collect for any amount <= that recorded balance must not revert.

For all inputs, the reference contract C never allows a holder to withdraw (Collect) an amount if their balance is below MinSum; the mutant removes the MinSum check and thus permits Collect when balance < MinSum for some inputs.

For any caller and amount, the reference C never allows Collect to succeed when the caller's balance is below MinSum; the mutant removes the MinSum check and so may allow Collect to succeed for callers with balance < MinSum.

For any caller, if their stored Acc[msg.sender].balance is < MinSum then calling Collect(_am) must always revert/refuse to transfer funds (i.e., Collect must not succeed); the mutant removing the MinSum check allows Collect to succeed for some inputs where balance < MinSum.

For every caller, Collect(_) never succeeds in transferring funds when the caller's recorded balance is below MinSum; the mutant removing the MinSum check can allow Collect to succeed for a caller whose balance < MinSum.

For all callers and amounts, the reference contract never allows a Collect to succeed (i.e., transfer Ether and reduce the caller's recorded balance) when the caller's stored balance is strictly less than MinSum; the mutant removes the MinSum check and thus can allow Collect to succeed for some inputs where stored balance < MinSum.
A holder cannot withdraw (Collect) an amount at a timestamp strictly less than the recorded unlockTime (i.e., Collect succeeds only when block.timestamp > stored unlockTime).

Collect never reverts when called with amount <= Acc[msg.sender].balance and block.timestamp > Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime and Acc[msg.sender].balance >= MinSum (i.e., withdrawal allowed only strictly after unlockTime).

If block.timestamp is exactly equal to the holder's unlockTime, Collect does not revert (i.e., is allowed) only in the mutant; in the original Collect, calls at timestamp == unlockTime must revert, so the test requires that Collect reverts when provided unlock time equal to current time and amount meeting minima.
If a caller's recorded unlockTime is strictly greater than the current block timestamp, Collect must revert (i.e., withdrawals are not allowed before unlockTime).
If the stored unlockTime for the caller is strictly greater than the current block timestamp, then Collect must revert.
